content: एतद् {%<ab>pron. a.</ab>%} ({%m.%}|एषः|{%f.%}|एषा|{%n.%}|एतद्) .²1 This, this here, yonder [referring to what is nearest to the speaker, (समीपतरवर्ति चैतदो रूपम); एते वयममी दाराः कन्येयं कुलजीवितम् <ls>K.</ls>; the <ab>Nom.</ab> forms are used like those of इदम् the sense of ‘here’; एष पृच्छामि, एष कथयामि <ls>Mu. 3</ls> here I ask <ab>&c.</ab>; कदा गमिष्यसि-एष गच्छामि <ls>Sk.</ls>; एषोऽस्मि कामन्दकी संवृत्तः <ls>Māl. 1</ls>; एते नवीकृताः स्मः <ls>Ś. 5</ls>. In this sense एतद् is sometimes used to give emphasis to the personal pronouns; एषोऽहं कार्यवशादायोध्यिकस्तदानींतनश्च संवृत्तः <ls>U. 1.</ls>] .²2 As the subject of a sentence it agrees in gender and number with the predicate without reference to the noun to which it refers; एतद् (शवला) मे धनम्; but many sometimes remain in the neuter; एतदेव गुरुषु वृत्तिः <ls>Ms. 2. 206</ls>. .²3 It often refers to what precedes, especially when it is joined with इदम् or any other pronoun; एष वै प्रथमः कल्पः <ls>Ms. 3. 147</ls>; इति यदुक्तं तदेतच्चिन्त्यम्; एतानीमानि, एते ते <ab>&c.</ab> .²4 It is used in connection with a relative clause, in which case the relative generally follows; प्रच्छन्नवञ्चकास्त्वेते ये स्तेनाटविकादयः <ls>Ms. 9. 257</ls>. --{%ind.%} In this manner, thus, so, here, at this time, now. {%Note%}:-- एतद् appears as the first member of compounds which are mostly self-explaining; {%<ab>e. g.</ab>%} ˚अतिरिक्त Besides this. ˚अनन्तर immediately after this; ˚अन्त ending thus; ˚अर्थः this matter; ˚अर्थे on this account, therefore; ˚अवधि to this limit, so far; ˚अवस्थ {%a.%} of such a state or condition.
